mainTopic: A minor's ability to acquire and to appoint agents, רבא's stages of a child, and agents for receiving or bringing a גט.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate over whether the rule 'whatever רבנן enacted, they modeled on Torah law' covers enactments with no Torah root. רב אויא then challenges שמואל's view that a קטן cannot acquire for others. He cites a משנה where a Hebrew maidservant, who must be a minor, redeems מעשר שני for her master. The גמרא first answers that the case is מעשר nowadays, which is only דרבנן. Since Hebrew servants do not exist nowadays, it moves the case to produce grown in an עציץ שאינו נקוב, which is also only rabbinic. רבא then lists three stages of a child's maturity and what a boy or girl can do legally at each stage. A new משנה teaches that a minor girl cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט, but her father can. It also covers what happens when a husband or wife names a place for the agent, where רבי אלעזר disagrees in the wife's case. The גמרא explains that the husband means his instruction, while the wife, who can be divorced against her will, is only giving directions. A final משנה applies these rules to when a כהן's wife must stop eating תרומה. The גמרא's answer to a contradiction there continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first sage's reason: rabbinic enactments copy Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the first sage: whatever רבנן enacted, they modeled on Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Whatever the רבנן enacted,] they enacted it in the pattern of Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started just before this section. It gives the reason of the first sage: רבנן build their enactments to look like Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבנן did not make up brand-new legal systems. When they made an enactment, they used the same rules the Torah uses. So if a קטן cannot acquire for others in Torah law, he cannot do so in a rabbinic setting either.

keyTerms.meaning: In the pattern of Torah law
They (the רבנן) enacted

phrases.english: they enacted in the pattern of Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the first sage's position from the preceding text.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rabbinic enactments follow the pattern of Torah law, so Torah rules about acquiring through a minor carry over.

steps.title: The other sage: the rule applies only to enactments rooted in Torah
steps.stepSummary: The second sage agrees that rabbinic enactments copy Torah law, but only when the topic has a root in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other sage holds: when we say that whatever the רבנן enacted follows the Torah's pattern, that applies to a matter that has a root in the Torah. But a matter with no root in the Torah does not follow that pattern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other sage acted differently. He limits the rule 'rabbinic enactments copy Torah law.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sages agree on the basic principle. They disagree about how far it reaches. The second sage says that for a purely rabbinic invention with no Torah base, the רבנן were free to set different rules, so a minor might be allowed to acquire there.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other sage)
A root or basis in the Torah
A matter, a thing

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept 'כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון.' The argument is only whether it covers enactments that have no Torah root.

phrases.english: And the other one: when we say:
whatever the Rabbis enacted
they enacted in the pattern of Torah law –

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִילְּתָא דְּאִית לַהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: that is for a matter that has a root in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִילְּתָא דְּלֵית לַהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה – לָא.
phrases.english: but a matter that has no root in the Torah – no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting reasoning of the second sage, limiting the principle stated in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle applies only to enactments with a Torah basis. Purely rabbinic matters may have their own rules.

steps.title: רב אויא's challenge from redeeming מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא quotes a משנה: a person may avoid the extra fifth on מעשר שני by giving money to his adult children or Hebrew servants to redeem it for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא objected: One may use a trick with מעשר שני. How? A person says to his adult son and daughter, or to his Hebrew slave and maidservant, 'Here is this money; redeem this מעשר שני with it.' Then he eats it without adding a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא brings a משנה to challenge שמואל's rule that a קטן cannot acquire for others. Here he just quotes the case; the next step shows why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner who redeems his own מעשר שני must add a fifth (חומש). If someone else redeems it with money they own, no fifth is needed. For the trick to work, the servants must truly acquire the money, and that is the detail the challenge will use.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection
We may use a legal trick
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money
The extra fifth added when an owner redeems his own produce
Hebrew (Jewish) servants

phrases.english: Rav Avya objected:
One may use a trick with second tithe.
How? A person says
to his adult son and daughter;
to his Hebrew slave and maidservant:
"Here is this money for you,
and redeem this second tithe with it,"
and he eats it without the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against שמואל's view that a minor cannot acquire for others.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a קטן cannot acquire on behalf of others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a Hebrew maidservant acquire money and redeem for her master; the next step shows she must be a minor.

steps.title: The maidservant must be a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the Hebrew maidservant in the משנה must be a minor, which seems to prove a minor can acquire for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this maidservant? If she has grown two hairs (she is an adult), what is she still doing with him? Rather, isn't it a case where she has not grown two hairs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב אויא's challenge. It proves the maidservant in the משנה must be a קטנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Hebrew maidservant goes free once she shows signs of adulthood. So if she is still serving, she must be a minor. Yet the משנה says she can acquire the money for redeeming, so it seems a minor can acquire for others, against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Two hairs: the physical sign of adulthood
Rather, isn't it…? (leads to a forced conclusion)

phrases.english: This maidservant, what is the case?
If she has grown two hairs,
what is she doing with him?
phrases.notes: A Hebrew maidservant goes free once she shows signs of adulthood, so she wouldn't still be his servant.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו דְּלָא אַתְיָא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת?
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it where she has not grown two hairs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 3 by proving the maidservant is a minor.
steps.raayaObject: That a קטן can acquire on behalf of others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעשר שני, where a Hebrew maidservant, who must be a minor, redeems for her master.

steps.title: The case is מעשר nowadays, which is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה deals with מעשר in our times, which is only דרבנן, so a minor may be allowed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With מעשר nowadays, which is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אויא's challenge. It limits the משנה to a case of rabbinic מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowadays מעשר is only a rabbinic obligation, so the רבנן could be lenient and let a minor's acquisition count. This does not prove that a minor can acquire for others in a Torah-level matter, so שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (limits a source to a specific case)
In our times (after the חורבן)
Rabbinic, not from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a first attempt to push the proof aside. Step 6 shows that the 'nowadays' setting cannot work. Step 7 keeps only the idea that the case is rabbinic.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a minor can acquire for others in general. It only says the משנה might be about a rabbinic case, so it cannot disprove שמואל.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
With tithe in our times – which is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 4 by limiting the משנה to rabbinic מעשר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה about the maidservant, without proving the opposite.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a Torah-level case. The משנה can be about rabbinic מעשר, where a minor's acquisition may be accepted.

steps.title: There are no Hebrew maidservants today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own answer: an אמה העבריה cannot exist in our times, because a ברייתא teaches that Hebrew servants exist only when the יובל is observed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there a Hebrew maidservant in our times?! A ברייתא teaches that the law of a Hebrew servant applies only when the יובל applies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in Step 5. If the משנה is about מעשר in our times, how can it mention a Hebrew maidservant, when those no longer exist?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the משנה is about מעשר today, which is only דרבנן. But the same משנה mentions an אמה העבריה. A ברייתא says Hebrew servants exist only when the יובל is in force, so the משנה cannot be describing our times.

keyTerms.meaning: In our times, after the יובל stopped being observed
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)
A Jewish servant who serves for a set period

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה מִי אִיכָּא?!
phrases.english: And is there a Hebrew maidservant in our times?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
The law of a Hebrew servant does not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee applies!
phrases.notes: The rule about the עבד עברי covers the אמה העבריה too, so she also can't exist today.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה מִי אִיכָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה deals with מעשר in our times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions an אמה העבריה, and she cannot exist when the יובל is not observed, so the case cannot be set in our times.

steps.title: The case is produce from a pot without a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the משנה deals with produce grown in a pot without a hole. Such produce owes מעשר only by rabbinic law, even in the times when Hebrew servants existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is about produce grown in a pot without a hole, which is only obligated by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the idea that the משנה is about a rabbinic case. It just finds a different rabbinic case that fits the times when Hebrew servants existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עציץ שאינו נקוב, a pot without a hole, keeps the produce cut off from the ground. So that produce owes מעשר only מדרבנן. This lets the משנה be set when the יובל was observed, so an אמה העבריה exists, while the מעשר is still only rabbinic. So the משנה still gives no proof that a minor can acquire for others in a Torah matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant pot with no hole at the bottom
Required by rabbinic law, not by Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה is still rejected. A minor acquiring for others may work in a rabbinic matter, and that does not show it works by Torah law.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about produce grown in a pot without a hole,
which is only rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 by moving the rabbinic case to a different setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbinic nature of the case came from it being set in our times
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic nature comes from the unperforated pot, so the case can be set when Hebrew servants existed

steps.title: רבא's first stage: the child who throws away a pebble but keeps a nut
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches the first of three stages of a minor. A child who can tell a pebble from a nut acquires for himself but not for others. A girl at the matching stage can be betrothed in a way she may later cancel by מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are three stages in a minor. A child who throws away a pebble but takes a nut acquires for himself, but not for others. A girl at the matching stage can be betrothed, subject to refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: The topic has been whether a minor can acquire, so the גמרא now brings רבא's list of a child's stages. This is the first stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child who knows a nut is worth keeping and a pebble is not understands enough to acquire for himself. He still cannot acquire on behalf of others. This fits the סוגיא's discussion of whether a minor can acquire for others.

keyTerms.meaning: A pebble
A nut
Acquires (gains legal ownership)
A minor girl
Refusal: a minor girl cancels a rabbinic marriage

phrases.english: Rava said: There are three stages in a minor:
if given a pebble he throws it away, and if given a nut he takes it,
he acquires for himself, but does not acquire for others;
and corresponding to them in a minor girl,
she can be betrothed, subject to refusal.
phrases.notes: This means a betrothal she can later undo by refusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by topic: after discussing a minor's ability to acquire, the גמרא brings רבא's stages of minors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the first stage a minor acquires for himself but not for others, and a girl can be betrothed subject to מיאון.

steps.title: Second stage: young children can buy and sell movables
steps.stepSummary: At the second stage, פעוטות can make real purchases and sales of movable items. A girl at the matching stage can receive her own גט, even from a betrothal her father arranged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Young children: their purchase is a purchase and their sale is a sale, for movable items. A girl at the matching stage can be divorced from a betrothal made by her father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves on to the second, more mature stage of a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the child's deals count, though only with מטלטלין. The matching girl can receive her גט herself, even though her father's betrothal is a Torah-level marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Young children, more mature than the first stage
Movable property
She is divorced (by receiving a גט)
A betrothal arranged by her father

phrases.english: Young children:
their purchase is a purchase and their sale is a sale, with movable property;
and corresponding to them in a minor girl,
she can be divorced from a betrothal made by her father.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפָּעוֹטוֹת מִקָּחָן מִקָּח וּמִמְכָּרָן מִמְכָּר בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list with the second stage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פעוטות can buy and sell movables, and a girl at that stage can receive a גט from her father's betrothal.

steps.title: Third stage: the age of vows, and selling a father's land at twenty
steps.stepSummary: At the third stage, the age of vows, a child's vows and הקדש count, and a girl at that stage can do חליצה. But selling land inherited from his father must wait until he is twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they reach the age of vows, their vows are vows and their consecration is consecration. A girl at the matching stage performs חליצה. But to sell his father's property, he must wait until he is twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the last and most mature stage of a minor. Then he adds a separate limit on selling a father's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At עונת נדרים, the child's vows and gifts to the Temple take effect. Even so, selling inherited land from his father needs much more maturity: he must be twenty, well past adulthood.

keyTerms.meaning: The age at which a child's vows take effect
Consecrating property to the Temple
She performs חליצה, the release from a יבום bond
His father's property, meaning inherited land

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's three stages: (1) pebble and nut: acquires for himself only; (2) פעוטות: buy and sell movables; (3) age of vows: vows and הקדש count. Selling a father's land waits until twenty.
steps.confusionAlert: Being twenty for selling a father's land means that for this one kind of sale he is still treated as a קטן until twenty, as רש״י says, even though he counts as an adult for other things.

phrases.english: Once they have reached the age of vows,
their vows are vows and their consecration is consecration;
and corresponding to them in a minor girl, she performs חליצה.
And to sell his father's property,
he must wait until he is twenty years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעוּ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים נִדְרֵיהֶן נֶדֶר וְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's list with the third stage and adds the age limit for selling a father's land
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the age of vows, a child's vows and הקדש take effect and a girl can do חליצה. Selling a father's land requires age twenty.

steps.title: A minor girl cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט
steps.stepSummary: If a minor girl tells an agent to receive her גט, the divorce does not happen until the גט reaches her hand. So the husband can still take it back, because a minor cannot appoint an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A minor girl said: 'Receive my גט for me.' It is not a divorce until the גט reaches her hand. So if the husband wants to take it back, he may, because a minor cannot appoint an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a minor girl's agent for receiving her גט is not a real agent for receiving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a woman's agent receives her גט, she is divorced right away and the husband can no longer cancel it. A minor cannot appoint an agent, so her 'agent' is really just a carrier. The divorce only happens once the גט is in her own hand, and until then the husband can still back out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
A minor girl
Receive my גט for me: the words that appoint an agent to receive
To take back, to cancel
Agent, messenger

steps.confusionAlert: Her words sound like she is appointing a real agent to receive. But since she is a minor, those words do nothing. He only works as a carrier who brings her the גט.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A minor girl who said:
"Receive my bill of divorce for me"

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גֵּט עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ גֵּט לְיָדָהּ;
phrases.english: it is not a divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her hand;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם רָצָה הַבַּעַל לַחֲזוֹר – יַחְזוֹר.
phrases.english: therefore, if the husband wants to take it back, he may take it back,
because a minor cannot appoint an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ קְטַנָּה שֶׁאָמְרָה הִתְקַבֵּל לִי גִּיטִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the גמרא's discussion of the minors' stages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's agent for receiving does not make the divorce take effect. The divorce happens only when the גט reaches her hand, so the husband may cancel until then.

steps.title: Her father can appoint an agent to receive her גט
steps.stepSummary: If the minor girl's father sends the agent to receive the גט, the divorce takes effect when the agent receives it. After that, the husband cannot take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if her father told the agent, 'Go and receive my daughter's גט for her,' and the husband then wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the girl with her father. When the father appoints the agent, it is a real agent for receiving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father has the power to receive a גט for his minor daughter. Because of this, he can also appoint someone else to receive it for her. Once that agent gets the גט, she is divorced, and the husband can no longer cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: Her father
He cannot take it back
An agent for receiving: once he gets the גט, she is divorced

phrases.english: But if her father said to him:
"Go and receive my daughter's bill of divorce for her,"
if the husband wants to take it back, he cannot take it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיהָ צֵא וְהִתְקַבֵּל לְבִתִּי גִּיטָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposite case to step 11: the father's appointment works where the girl's own does not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent sent by the father is a real agent for receiving. Once he receives the גט, the husband cannot cancel it.

steps.title: The husband names a place: an instruction versus just information
steps.stepSummary: If the husband says 'Give it to my wife in place X' and the agent gives it elsewhere, the גט is invalid. If he only says 'She is in place X,' giving it elsewhere is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'Give this גט to my wife in such-and-such a place,' and the agent gave it to her somewhere else, it is invalid. If he said, 'She is in such-and-such a place,' and the agent gave it to her somewhere else, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic. It asks what happens when an agent hands over the גט somewhere other than the place the husband mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Give it to her in place X' is a real instruction. If the agent breaks it, he has gone beyond what he was sent to do, so the גט is invalid. 'She is in place X' just tells the agent where to find her and sets no condition, so giving it elsewhere is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Such-and-such a place: a specific place that was named
A different place
Invalid
Valid
Here she is, meaning 'she is located in'

phrases.english: One who says: "Give this bill of divorce to my wife
in such-and-such a place,"
and the agent gave it to her in another place: it is invalid.
If he said: "She is in such-and-such a place,"
and the agent gave it to her in another place: it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר תֵּן גֵּט זֶה לְאִשְׁתִּי בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in the same משנה: where the agent delivers the גט, instead of who appointed him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband names a place as an instruction, giving the גט anywhere else makes it invalid. If he names the place only to say where she is, giving it elsewhere is valid.

steps.title: The wife names a place for her agent: a dispute, then the 'bring' case
steps.stepSummary: If the wife tells her agent to receive the גט in place X and he receives it elsewhere, the first opinion says it is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid. If she tells him to bring it from place X and he brings it from elsewhere, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman said, 'Receive my גט for me in such-and-such a place,' and the agent received it somewhere else. It is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid. If she said, 'Bring me my גט from such-and-such a place,' and he brought it from somewhere else, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now looks at the wife's side. It asks what happens when her agent does not go to the place she named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she appoints an agent to receive, the divorce happens the moment he gets the גט. So the first opinion treats the place she named as a real condition, and breaking it makes the גט invalid. רבי אלעזר disagrees and holds it is valid. When she only says 'bring,' the divorce does not happen until the גט reaches her hand, so where the agent picked it up does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the first opinion in this משנה
Rules it valid
Bring me: appoints an agent who only carries the גט to her
An agent for carrying: she is divorced only when the גט reaches her

steps.whatToRemember: Who appointed the agent, and what words were used, decide when the divorce takes effect. 'Receive for me' (by an adult woman or by the father) makes it take effect when the agent gets the גט. 'Bring me,' or a minor's own appointment, makes it take effect only when the גט reaches her hand. A place that is named as a real instruction must be followed.

phrases.english: A woman who said:
"Receive my bill of divorce for me in such-and-such a place,"
and he received it for her in another place: it is invalid;
Rabbi Elazar rules it valid.
If she said: "Bring me my bill of divorce from such-and-such a place,"
and he brought it to her from another place: it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה הִתְקַבֵּל לִי גִּיטִּי בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This matches step 13, but now it is the wife, not the husband, who names the place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If her agent for receiving goes to a different place, the first opinion says the גט is invalid and רבי אלעזר says it is valid. If her agent was only told to bring the גט, getting it from a different place is valid.

steps.title: Why does רבי אלעזר argue only in the second case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר agrees in the husband's case but disagrees in the wife's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר: why does he not argue in the first case, where the husband named a place, but does argue in the second case, where the wife named a place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבי אלעזר's opinion in the last משנה. It wants to know why he treats the husband's place-instruction and the wife's place-instruction differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the husband's place-instruction is strict, and רבי אלעזר is silent, so he agrees. In the second case, the wife's place-instruction is broken and רבי אלעזר says the גט is still valid. The גמרא wants to know what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason two cases are treated differently
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
He disagrees

phrases.english: Gemara: And according to Rabbi Elazar,
what is different about the first clause, where he does not disagree,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the husband's case: "Give it to my wife in place X" (step 13).

phrases.english: and what is different about the latter clause, where he disagrees?
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the wife's case: "Receive it for me in place X" (step 14).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא פְּלִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רבי אלעזר's opinion, which was stated in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי אלעזר treats a husband's place-instruction as binding but not a wife's.

steps.title: The husband means it; the wife is only showing a place
steps.stepSummary: The husband divorces by his own choice, so he truly cares about the place. The wife is divorced even against her will, so her place-instruction is only directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He divorces by his own will, so he is strict about his instructions. She can be divorced even against her will, so she is only showing the agent where to find the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Each person's power over the divorce decides how seriously we take their place-instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband decides whether a divorce happens at all, so his conditions are real conditions, and breaking them ruins the גט. The wife cannot stop the divorce, so she has no real power to set conditions. When she names a place, she is just giving directions, and receiving the גט somewhere else does not hurt it.

keyTerms.meaning: By his own will or choice
He is strict about it and really means it
Against her will
Just pointing out a place, giving directions

steps.whatToRemember: The husband's place-instruction is a real condition. For רבי אלעזר, the wife's place-instruction is only directions, because a woman can be divorced against her will.

phrases.english: He, who divorces by his own will, is strict about it;
she, who is divorced against her will,
is only showing him a place.
phrases.notes: She is just telling the agent where the husband can be found, not making it a condition.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband controls the divorce, so his place-instruction is a real condition. The wife cannot block the divorce, so her place-instruction is only directions.

steps.title: When must the wife of a כהן stop eating תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: With a delivery agent, she eats תרומה until the גט reaches her. With a receiving agent, she must stop right away. If she named a place, the תנא קמא lets her eat until the גט reaches that place, but רבי אלעזר forbids it right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says "Bring me my גט," she may eat תרומה until the גט reaches her hand. If she says "Receive my גט for me," she may not eat תרומה from that moment. If she says "Receive my גט for me in place X," she may eat תרומה until the גט reaches that place. רבי אלעזר forbids her right away.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It applies the two kinds of agents to a practical question: when does a woman married to a כהן lose her right to eat תרומה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A delivery agent works for the husband, so nothing happens until the גט is in her hand. A receiving agent works for her, and the divorce happens once he gets the גט, which could happen at any moment, so she must stop right away. When she named a place, the תנא קמא assumes he will receive it only there. רבי אלעזר, who holds that she was only giving directions, worries he may already have received it anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן; his wife may eat it while married
"Bring me my גט": a delivery agent
"Receive my גט for me": a receiving agent
Immediately

steps.confusionAlert: "Bring" and "receive" sound alike but are very different. With "bring," she is still married until the גט is in her hand. With "receive," she may already be divorced before the agent comes back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the choice of agent decides the exact moment the divorce happens, and that moment has real effects on her daily life.

phrases.english: Mishnah: If she says "Bring me my bill of divorce,"
she may eat teruma
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about a woman married to a כהן. She may eat תרומה only while she is still married.

phrases.english: until the bill of divorce reaches her hand.
If she says "Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
she is forbidden to eat teruma immediately.
If she says "Receive my bill of divorce for me in such and such a place,"

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶלֶת בִּתְרוּמָה עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ גֵּט לְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: she may eat teruma until the bill of divorce reaches that place;
Rabbi Elazar forbids her immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָבֵא לִי גִּיטִּי – אוֹכֶלֶת בִּתְרוּמָה עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ גֵּט לְיָדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that uses the agent rules from steps 11-14 to decide when she must stop eating תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delivery agent: she eats תרומה until the גט is in her hand. Receiving agent: she must stop immediately. Receiving agent with a named place: the תנא קמא says she may eat until the גט reaches that place, while רבי אלעזר says she must stop immediately.

steps.title: But didn't the earlier משנה call this גט invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. Here he seems to treat a גט received elsewhere as valid once it reaches the named place, but earlier he said such a גט is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it a valid גט at all? But you said in the earlier משנה that it is not a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the new משנה with a challenge. The new משנה seems to contradict what the תנא קמא said in the earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new משנה says she may eat until the גט reaches the named place, which suggests it works once it gets there, even if it was received somewhere else. But in step 14, the תנא קמא said that if the agent received it somewhere other than the place she named, the גט is invalid. So how can it become valid here?

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate, at all
But you said! Points to an earlier statement that seems to clash
It is not a valid גט

phrases.english: Gemara: And is it a bill of divorce at all?
But you said in the first clause,
phrases.notes: "The first clause" here means the earlier משנה from step 14, where she named a place.

phrases.english: that it is not a bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא's ruling in the משנה of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling in step 17 that she may eat תרומה until the גט reaches the named place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ruling suggests a גט received elsewhere becomes valid once it reaches the named place. But in step 14, the same תנא קמא said a גט received somewhere other than the place she named is invalid.

steps.title: She explicitly allowed taking the גט anywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא's תרומה ruling is about a woman who named מתא מחסיא but told the agent he may take the גט from the husband wherever he finds him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where she told him: 'Receive my גט in מתא מחסיא, and sometimes you might find him in בבל.' This is what she means: as for taking it, wherever you find him, take it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to the contradiction by describing a special case where the wife herself allowed the agent to take the גט anywhere. The second half of her instruction continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the תנא קמא said a גט received somewhere other than the named place is not valid. That ruling was about a woman who limited her agent to one place. Here she openly told the agent he may take the גט from the husband wherever he finds him, so taking it in בבל is allowed. The second half of her instruction continues on the next amud, and it explains why she may still eat תרומה until the גט reaches the named place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed except for...' — the case is narrowed to a specific situation
A town in Babylonia, the place the woman named
Sometimes
Taking (the גט): the physical act of receiving it
Take it from him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is going back on the earlier rule. A גט taken outside the named place is still not valid when she limited the agent to that place. This case is different only because she openly allowed taking it anywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a woman's place instruction can cover two separate things: where the גט may be physically taken, and something else that the next amud spells out. Separating them is what removes the contradiction.

phrases.english: No, it is needed [only for a case]
where she said to him (the agent):
"Receive the bill of divorce for me in מתא מחסיא,
and sometimes you will find him (the husband) in בבל";
phrases.notes: Here בבל means a separate city, not all of Babylonia.

phrases.english: and this is what she is saying to him:
as for taking it: anywhere that you find him,
take it from him;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by limiting the תנא קמא's תרומה ruling to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ruling applies only where she explicitly allowed taking the גט anywhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא seemed to accept a גט taken outside the named place, which contradicts his earlier ruling that such a גט is not valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case she openly allowed the agent to take the גט from the husband wherever he finds him, so taking it elsewhere is valid. The earlier ruling still applies when she limited him to one place.
